name: Tax Identification Number (TIN)
note: Antigua and Barbuda's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: TINs aren't issued automatically to individuals; the Inland Revenue Department's tax software (SIGTAS) assigns one at the end of registration, numbers only, the smallest 6 digits (a check digit only for VAT (ABST) registrants, not modelled; a tax account number adds a two-digit tax-type code). The game draws the 6-digit form, the shortest the sheet names, since it gives no fixed length. Read as given on application (registration), to anyone registering; `needed` is tax. No age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Antigua and Barbuda: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Individuals No Entities No ... TIN s are assigned at the end of the registration process by our Tax Administration software (SIGTAS), with the smallest number being 6 digits. TINs only contain numbers.
